Definition: diminutive from κηός (wax); a cell for honey, i.e. (collectively) the comb:--(honey-)comb.
BiblicalUsage: Kerion means a honeycomb, the comb of the hive. Luke 24:42 says they gave the risen Jesus a piece of a broiled fish, and of an honeycomb.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the risen Lord ate fish and honey to prove he was no ghost: he has a body, and it is hungry.
